title: Migdal electrons and bremsstrahlung photons accompanying a 248 keV xenon recoil: extra quanta, their shift in S1-S2, and the -1.5 sigma band position
question: How often does a 248 keV Xe recoil carry Migdal inner-shell ionisation or a nuclear-bremsstrahlung photon, how much ER energy follows, where does it move the event in (S1c, log10 S2c) in NR-band sigma, can it explain the -1.5 sigma position, and what makes an NR charge-poor?
headline_result: M-shell Migdal hole in 0.6-1.4 % of 248 keV recoils (L 6e-4, K 1.6e-5, brems >1 keV 7e-5), each lifting the event UP by +2.9 to +18 sigma; wrong sign for the -1.5 sigma position, ~1e-3 acceptance loss; the charge-poor position remains a 6 % recombination fluctuation (P024).
key_numbers: v_A 604 km/s, q_e 1.03 keV; P(K/L/M/brems) 1.6e-5/5.9e-4/9.6e-3/7.2e-5; <E_ER> 55/8.0/1.26 keV; shifts +0.39/+1.67/+2.57/+5.6/+14.4 sigma for 0.1/0.5/1/5/35 keV; +2 sigma at 0.65 keV, ROI at 2.7 keV; 1.1 % above +2 sigma, 0.10 % above ROI; Migdal+brems mean 31 eV = 4e-4 of electronic energy
model_or_mechanism: Migdal effect (dipole closure sum rule + oscillator-strength route), nuclear bremsstrahlung with Z_eff(w) screening, NR+ER quanta addition in NEST
agent_tools: Read x11, Bash x13, Write x5, Edit x15, Skill x1 (dataviz)
